customManagers.description: Bump the Go tools the Makefile builds under .tools, each marked with a 'renovate:' comment on the line above its pin. Go module tags carry the v the Makefile writes, so the matched value is reused as is.

packageRules.description: Every bump lands as 'build' so it appears under the Dependencies changelog section, which release-please treats as releasable: a bumped module is a new binary for every plugin whose go.mod moved, and it reaches nobody without a release.
The Go toolchain is the go directive in every plugin's go.mod and the pin in mise.toml. One pull request moves them all.

Non-major Go module bumps across the plugins land together: one commit and one round of patch releases a week rather than one per module per plugin. A vulnerable module skips both the grouping and the schedule through the OSV alerts above. This repository's own modules are left out, for the rule below.

A plugin that serves another plugin's package, as mariadb serves the family package of plugins/mysql, pins that plugin's release, so a release of it reaches the other plugin only through this bump: on its own, and as soon as the release exists rather than the next Monday beside unrelated modules.

The SDK is compiled into every binary and every plugin follows an rta release: bump-rta.yml opens that pull request from the release itself, carrying its notes, and it has to be the only thing that does.
Reusable workflows are called at the moving v0 major tag on purpose until github-workflows reaches v1 - don't pin or bump them.
